The rival kingdoms of Timur's descendants in Transoxiana, Khorasan and Afghanistan in the late 15th century, the last phase of the Timurid Empire. The map shows them in 1492 and 1500.

After Timur's son Shah Rukh died in 1447, the empire broke apart among princes in Samarkand, Herat, Ferghana and Kabul. Politics was weak, but culture flourished. In Herat, Sultan Husayn Bayqara, who ruled from 1469 to 1506, kept a brilliant court: the poet Ali-Shir Nava'i wrote in Chagatai Turkic, and Behzad painted the finest Persian miniatures of the age.

The end came from the north. Muhammad Shaybani led the Uzbeks south, took Samarkand around 1500 and Herat in 1507. One young Timurid, Babur of Ferghana, lost Samarkand to him, moved to Kabul and in 1526 founded the Mughal Empire in India, which carried the Timurid line on for three more centuries.
